title: Late Breaking Results: Extracting QNNs from NISQ Computers via Ensemble Learning
problem: Model extraction attacks on quantum neural networks deployed on NISQ computers produce low-quality local substitute QNNs due to quantum noise. Existing extraction attacks designed for classical models are ineffective at handling the noise characteristics of near-term quantum computers.
motivation: As quantum computing platforms become deployed through cloud services, protecting quantum neural networks from model extraction attacks is critical for security and intellectual property protection.
method: The approach applies bagging-based ensemble learning to QNN extraction. Multiple independent weak learners are trained using outputs from repeated black-box queries to the victim QNN. These ensemble learners are aggregated to mimic the victim QNN while improving robustness to NISQ noise, treating quantum noise similar to how bagging handles training data noise.
key_novelty: Applying bagging-based ensemble learning to improve quantum neural network extraction from NISQ computers by treating quantum noise like data noise.
contributions: Novel QNN extraction approach using bagging-based ensemble learning
15.09% accuracy improvement over previous extraction techniques
Demonstrated effectiveness on NISQ computers despite quantum noise
Bridge connecting classical ensemble methods to quantum model extraction
limitations: Limitations not discussed in this late-breaking results submission.
primary_theme: Ensemble learning for noise-robust QNN extraction
